articles.title: Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Argon to Trusted Cyber Defenders, Plans Guardrail-Free Version
articles.text:
Google on Wednesday announced its latest frontier artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini 4 Argon, that it said is being rolled out to a set of trusted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program.
"It delivers frontier performance in complex workflows across real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense," Koray Kavukcuoglu, senior vice president of Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect at Google, said.
The development comes nearly a month after the tech giant unveiled Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, which it described as the most capable cybersecurity model.
Like similar models from rivals Anthropic and OpenAI, Argon is assessed to be highly capable at autonomously finding, validating, and patching critical software vulnerabilities.
This includes a previously unknown critical vulnerability exposing sensitive personal information across healthcare software used by hospitals worldwide. Google did not reveal which software was affected by the security flaw.
Argon, according to Google, demonstrates "impressive leaps" in vulnerability discovery over 3.8 Flash Cyber, and outperforms the model when it comes to discovering the attack surface and generating proof-of-concepts (PoCs) to validate the findings.
Google said it plans to release a version of Argon without cyber guardrails to trusted defenders and its internal teams so that they can take advantage of its full capabilities.
Ahead of a broader rollout, the company said it's working to strengthen safeguards to rein in misalignment, prevent model misuse by bad actors, and make it resilient to indirect prompt injections (IPIs). According to a model evaluation released by Google, Argon outperforms other models to take the top spot in the Gray Swan's IPI benchmark.
"We are deploying misalignment mitigations that monitor Argon’s chain-of-thought and actions and stop execution when necessary," Google said. "We strongly encourage the rest of the industry to preserve reasoning transparency in these pivotal moments of increased capabilities while navigating alignment risks, so that model thoughts remain helpful in identifying and diagnosing misalignment."

articles.title: Brian Chesky interview: AI agents need their own operating system | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Airbnb rolled out its new AI-powered search this week as part of its fall update, a significant step for a company that has been slow and deliberate about AI. Co-founder and CEO Brian Chesky has said in the past that a chatbot-only interface is not fit for travel discovery. With more AI on the way to the Airbnb app, I caught up with Chesky over Zoom to talk about how the company is approaching it, where interfaces are headed, why consumer AI still isn’t working, and what role voice will play.
Chesky hasn’t changed his mind on chatbots. He said they aren’t good for browsing or shopping because they give you a few options at a time, and you have to take multiple turns before reaching a result. But he doesn’t see the current version of Airbnb’s search as the final form either: its interface will evolve over time.
“I think that I’ve believed for a long time that a chatbot isn’t the right interface for e-commerce. I think what you’re seeing today is also not the endgame for e-commerce or for travel or shopping. I think that there’s going to be some interface that is, you know, I don’t want to call it a midpoint, but something between a chatbot and what you see in the first version we shipped,” he said.
Continued Chesky: “You know, a lot of people want some things … to be fast and easy, like ‘Book me a flight, I don’t want to look at it.’ With Airbnb, they enjoy looking at the product. Travel studies show that people actually derive more pleasure in planning and anticipating travel than they do traveling. So you don’t want to take the inspiration and the browsing and the library experience of dreaming away.”
Chesky sees a second problem with chatbots, which is that they are built for one person. He feels that they aren’t a collaborative interface, which matters for a product that people often use with family and friends. Over the next three to six months, the company’s task is to explore interfaces that enable “multiplayer” AI, meaning AI that several people, such as a group planning a trip together, can use at once.
Airbnb isn’t the only one rethinking what an AI interface should look like. As AI tools evolve, new interfaces are also showing up in apps. Startups like Monogram and, more recently, Wabi are experimenting with “generative” interfaces, which are screens an AI builds on-the-fly rather than ones a designer fixed in advance. Chesky thinks people will see a mix of deterministic (pre-designed and predictable) and generative interfaces.
I asked Chesky how Airbnb is preparing for consumer AI agents, which are tools like Instinct and Muse that carry out tasks on a person’s behalf. Agents will need robust software infrastructure on Airbnb’s end, he said, and the company wants to make itself more agent-friendly. In his view, they could be good lead generators.
“I don’t necessarily know if I believe in a world that there’s apps in the future, but I don’t believe in a world where the apps become data layers of a universal simple UI because when you open your iPhone, there is a reason Airbnb’s app is a different design than DoorDash, Shopify, and Amazon. Our interfaces should be adaptive to the utility and the function that we’re doing. We want to make our app more agentic, and we want to build a lot more user interface controls,” he said.
“If I have an agent, but I also want like really great browse functionality, if I want to be able to message the host like an Airbnb, if I want to be able to compare, if I want to be able to verify my identity, if I want to be able to use a map feature, if I want to then be able to add other items, then if I want to stay in the platform, then either the agent has to do a handoff or the agent application would need to build a bit more of, I think, a robust software developer kit to bring the app to you, so to speak.”
Chesky thinks that there were concerns around AI tools cutting companies like Airbnb out of the customer relationship, but he said that chatbots have proven to be good at lead generation.
The Airbnb CEO is also planning for agent-to-agent interactions through the platform. He explained there might be some interactions within the platform and some with agents of other apps. His thesis is that apps have not always been interoperable unless companies struck a business deal. On the other hand, agents are like “apps with faces,” and when they talk to each other, all apps can become interoperable.
“I think of the Airbnb app as one day becoming an agent, you know, where basically the explore tab has an agent, our customer service has an agent, we’re developing another agent in another service area. Probably eventually there’s going to be a macro Airbnb agent. And that will probably be interoperable with MCP [a standard that lets AI agents connect with other software] to other agents,” Chesky noted.
Chesky argues the bigger problem is that the industry lacks a true operating system built for AI. Right now people are building AI apps for iOS, macOS, and Windows that are not “AI operating systems.” He thinks that in an ideal world, AI would be operable at the kernel level — the core of an operating system — and all components like agents would interact with each other. Right now, he said, the race is to be the “quarterback,” or primary AI agent that users go through for everything.
“The problem with that model [of trying to become primary agent] is no one is developing a full operating system software developer kit. I’ll give you an example,” he continued. “ChatGPT, at the beginning of last year, tried to do their little app store. And I told Sam [Altman]: If you want to be an app store like the iPhone, you need to have a software developer kit and an operating system like the App Store. Otherwise, none of our functionality is going to exist. And of course, it didn’t work very well,” Chesky said.
“I’ve used Airbnb on Muse and Instinct,” he went on. “And it doesn’t work very well. I mean, even hotels don’t work that well, but Airbnbs work even worse. So I don’t think we’ve cracked consumer AI. And for consumer AI to be cracked, we have to crack at a lower substrate, and we need to make the agents [into] apps; all apps need to become agents; all must be interoperable; and all must have much richer user interfaces.”
Chesky thinks that there are two misconceptions in Silicon Valley: first, that the interface is going away and people will just talk and type; second, that software will be completely generative. His argument is that a designer can prompt better software than a consumer can.
He also thinks that as long as the iPhone remains dominant and Apple and Google control the major platforms, apps will likely remain a central fixture.
“It’s really up to Apple or Google, or somebody, to build a new platform for us to really make the true shift from apps to agents. Otherwise, we’re going to have apps that have agents inside them, rather than the whole app being a robust agent that’s interoperable with other agents,” he said.
Before we wrapped up, I asked Chesky about voice, which is gaining ground as apps like Wispr Flow, Willow, and Superwhisper, a new wave of note-taking apps, and built-in dictation in AI tools get people talking to their devices more. He thinks people will eventually speak to computers more than they type. Voice, he said, will play a key part for Airbnb in search and customer service, and the company plans to roll out voice agents this fall to help users.
The company has also been seeing big gains from using AI to ship features faster, he volunteered. On a personal level, Chesky said AI has helped him get information faster, freeing him from so many meetings.
“I think AI is reducing communication layers. One of my jobs as CEO is try to get information. And the way I used to get information was having meetings. Now, I can just ask my AI and I don’t need to have as many,” he said.

articles.title: OpenAI demite pesquisadores após vazamento de informações restritas
articles.text:
A OpenAI demitiu três pesquisadores de sua equipe de segurança por suposta má conduta, incluindo o compartilhamento de informações confidenciais da empresa com uma organização externa dedicada à segurança de inteligência artificial (IA), segundo pessoas familiarizadas com o assunto ouvidas pelo The Wall Street Journal.
A empresa informou recentemente a alguns funcionários que havia encerrado o vínculo com três pesquisadores que trabalhavam na área de segurança. Os profissionais são Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak e Mikita Balesni.
Em comunicado, um porta-voz da OpenAI afirmou que os três foram desligados por violarem políticas relacionadas ao acesso e ao tratamento de informações confidenciais.
“Encerramos a relação com três indivíduos por violarem nossas políticas sobre acesso e tratamento de informações confidenciais da empresa. Nossa investigação confirmou que essas pessoas manipularam informações sensíveis fora dos procedimentos estabelecidos pela empresa, violando nossas políticas e quebrando a confiança essencial ao nosso trabalho”, afirmou.
Os pesquisadores não comentaram suas demissões.
Caso Hugging Face está no centro da questão
- As demissões ocorrem enquanto a OpenAI enfrenta uma série de incidentes envolvendo agentes de IA que apresentaram comportamentos fora do controle esperado;
- Depois que um modelo da empresa invadiu a plataforma de IA Hugging Face, a OpenAI permitiu que integrantes da organização de segurança de IA METR e um pesquisador da Redwood Research, contratado pelo grupo, trabalhassem durante seis dias dentro de seus escritórios para investigar o comportamento dos modelos;
- Posteriormente, a METR publicou um relatório baseado nas informações às quais teve acesso durante a investigação;
- Um dos pesquisadores demitidos, Tomek Korbak, fazia parte da equipe de segurança da OpenAI e já havia afirmado que atuava como contato técnico da empresa com a Redwood Research e a METR durante a investigação do incidente envolvendo a Hugging Face;
- Jasmine Wang e Mikita Balesni trabalhavam na área de alinhamento, campo dedicado a fazer com que os modelos de IA se comportem de acordo com as intenções humanas.
Empresas de IA enfrentam pressão por testes independentes
O episódio acontece em momento de pressão crescente para que grandes empresas de IA submetam seus sistemas a avaliações independentes de segurança.
No mês passado, o CEO da Anthropic, Dario Amodei, afirmou que a empresa permitiria que avaliadores externos, como a METR, verificassem sua adesão a medidas de segurança e avaliassem o alinhamento de seus modelos.
A OpenAI, por sua vez, vem investigando uma série de incidentes de segurança envolvendo seus agentes de IA. Segundo a empresa, alguns desses sistemas escaparam das limitações previstas, invadiram determinados sites e realizaram sondagens agressivas em uma ampla variedade de páginas.
A companhia afirmou que está investigando diferentes incidentes identificados nos últimos meses e trabalhando para solucionar problemas de segurança subjacentes.
OpenAI reforça medidas de segurança
Em meio aos episódios, a OpenAI afirmou ter implementado novo sistema de monitoramento para identificar mais rapidamente comportamentos inadequados de agentes de IA.
A empresa também passou a exigir que engenheiros utilizem mecanismos de proteção mais fortes durante os testes de seus sistemas de inteligência artificial. Outra medida anunciada é o compartilhamento de mais informações sobre situações em que os modelos apresentam comportamentos considerados inadequados.
No início desta semana, a OpenAI também cancelou o lançamento planejado de um modelo de IA chamado GPT-6.1 Astra por preocupações relacionadas à segurança.
O setor de IA enfrenta, assim, cenário de crescente preocupação com as capacidades dos modelos mais avançados e os riscos associados a sistemas capazes de executar tarefas com maior autonomia.
Leia mais:
- E aconteceu de novo: agentes de IA tentaram invadir site do governo do Canadá
- OpenAI: agentes de IA podem ter afetado mais de 100 organizações
- OpenAI: Califórnia abre investigação após agentes de IA invadirem sistemas
Debate sobre ritmo de desenvolvimento
As preocupações também atingiram outras empresas do setor.
No início de setembro, o pesquisador da Anthropic, Jacob Coxon, deixou a empresa publicamente. Segundo ele, não queria participar de uma corrida para desenvolver sistemas de IA capazes de melhorar a si próprios.
Coxon afirmou temer que essas tecnologias pudessem sair de controle e provocar consequências catastróficas.
No mês passado, Dario Amodei escreveu que os riscos apresentados pelas ferramentas de IA de ponta eram grandes demais para que o desenvolvimento continuasse no ritmo acelerado observado atualmente.
O executivo defendeu desaceleração do desenvolvimento da indústria de forma geral. A posição recebeu concordância do CEO da OpenAI, Sam Altman, e de Elon Musk.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Android Central ‘will continue’ despite laying off its staff
articles.text:
Android Central, a blog focused on the Android ecosystem, laid off its staff yesterday, but owner Future confirms to The Verge that the site will continue publishing.
Android Central ‘will continue’ despite laying off its staff
The Android-focused blog is still publishing posts even though all of its full-time staff were cut.
Yesterday, four of the six staffers on Android Central’s staff page posted publicly about the layoffs, including Shruti Shekar, Derrek Lee, Harish Jonnalagadda, and Nicholas Sutrich, and former senior editor Namerah Saud Fatmi updated her LinkedIn to indicate that her tenure at Android Central had ended. Both Lee, the site’s managing editor, and Sutrich confirmed that all remaining staff were laid off.
The former staffers weren’t told whether the site would shut down. Today, new posts have been published to the site, though they are from the site’s freelance contributors rather than the previous full-time staffers.
“Future will continue to publish Android Central. We’ll share further information about the future of the site in due course,” Future spokesperson Nicole Martineau tells The Verge, adding: “We will not be providing any further comment at this time.”
Android Police, another Android-focused blog, also laid off at least two staffers recently. The site currently lists an editorial team of four people. Valnet, which owns Android Police and previously purchased The Verge’s sister site Polygon, didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

articles.title: NordVPN, Proton VPN, ExpressVPN et Surfshark dans le viseur de LaLiga dans une liste anti-piratage européenne
articles.text:
LaLiga veut faire inscrire quatre grands services VPN dans la prochaine Counterfeit and Piracy Watch List de la Commission européenne. La ligue espagnole vise surtout la manière dont certains sites affiliés présentent ces outils pour contourner des blocages judiciaires visant des sites pirates, mais aussi certaines restrictions géographiques.
NordVPN, Proton VPN, ExpressVPN et Surfshark apparaissent dans la contribution adressée par LaLiga à la Commission européenne pour préparer sa Counterfeit and Piracy Watch List 2027. La demande ne porte pas directement sur le principe des VPN. LaLiga vise plutôt leur promotion commerciale via certains sites affiliés, avec deux griefs distincts.
LaLiga vise surtout le contournement des blocages judiciaires
Le principal concerne des pages affiliées qui citent des sites de streaming pirates et expliquent qu’un VPN permet de contourner les blocages ordonnés par les tribunaux. LaLiga affirme que c’est cette exploitation commerciale de la capacité à contourner des mesures judiciaires qui justifie l’inscription des quatre services dans la Watch List.
Autre grief, moins directement lié au piratage : certains guides expliquent comment utiliser un VPN pour contourner les restrictions géographiques et accéder à des retransmissions légalement disponibles dans d’autres pays. LaLiga y voit une atteinte à l’exclusivité territoriale de ses contrats de diffusion.
L’organisation estime également que certains contenus affiliés ne sont pas totalement indépendants. Elle cite notamment vpnMentor, relié à Kape Technologies, propriétaire d’ExpressVPN, l’un des quatre services visés. LaLiga reconnaît toutefois que ces publications déclarent ce lien de propriété. Sa contribution ne fournit par ailleurs aucun lien précis vers un guide ou un influenceur particulier qui aurait franchi la ligne.
Une offensive déjà engagée en Espagne
Cette démarche européenne prolonge un combat déjà engagé devant la justice espagnole. En février, un tribunal de Cordoue a ordonné à NordVPN et Proton VPN de bloquer certaines adresses IP associées à des retransmissions pirates, dans le cadre d’une procédure d’urgence menée sans que les deux fournisseurs soient entendus.
En mai, ce même tribunal a toutefois refusé de sanctionner NordVPN pour non-respect de l’ordonnance, tandis que la procédure principale reste en cours.
L’inscription éventuelle de VPN dans la Watch List constituerait aussi un précédent, comme le souligne Torrent Freak. La précédente édition, publiée en 2025, citait déjà des hébergeurs, IPFS ou encore Njalla, mais aucun fournisseur VPN. 
La nuance reste essentielle : la Commission européenne rappelle que cette liste ne constitue pas un constat d’illégalité. La consultation principale s’est achevée le 21 septembre, mais les parties prenantes peuvent encore répondre aux contributions reçues jusqu’au 28 octobre 2026. La liste définitive doit être publiée au deuxième trimestre 2027. 
Autrement dit, l’Union européenne n’a pour l’instant placé aucun de ces VPN sur une liste noire. C’est LaLiga qui demande leur inscription, avec derrière cette offensive une question de fond : jusqu’où un fournisseur peut-il être tenu responsable de la manière dont ses partenaires font la promotion de son service ?

articles.title: flydubai pilot 'a hero', plumber steadied plunging aircraft: Trump
articles.text:
flydubai pilot 'a hero', plumber steadied plunging aircraft: Trump
The pilot who staved off the attempt to crash the aircraft has been identified as Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, and hailed a "hero" by Netanyahu and many others.
US President Donald Trump hailed the flydubai pilot as a "hero" for fighting off a knife attack from the co-pilot, opening the cockpit door and calling for help to foil a bid to crash the aircraft.
Interacting with reporters at the Oval Office, Trump said he spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who told him that a plumber, who had never flown an aircraft, made a dramatic intervention to steady the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight which landed in Saudi Arabia.
The pilot who staved off the attempt to crash the aircraft has been identified as Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, and hailed a "hero" by Netanyahu and many others.
"The pilot was in very bad shape; I guess he still is in very bad shape, but he had the sense to, amazing, to, in a way he was a hero," Trump said, recalling his conversation with Netanyahu.
Trump said the pilot opened the door and was able to fall back, get the door open and scream for help.
"It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job, and he stabbed the pilot," the US President said.
Trump then described what he called an "amazing" intervention by an Israeli passenger whom he identified as a plumber.
Trump said a passenger, who had never flown an aircraft, entered the cockpit, pulled the co-pilot out of his seat and threw him backwards, where other passengers helped restrain him.
According to Trump, the passenger later said he had learned some basic concepts about flying from watching the television program Air Disasters.
"He said he watches it a lot, and he learned from watching that show sort of how to fly," Trump said.
Trump said additional pilots and security personnel, who had been toward the rear of the aircraft, subsequently reached the cockpit and took control.
"I think it’s the most amazing story," he said.
However, Trump said that he was merely recounting an account he had received rather than independently confirmed facts.
"Now this is the story that I heard. I don’t know if it’s true, but that’s the story that I got from Bibi and from a couple of probably early (sources)," he said.

articles.title: Efecto Cristiano Ronaldo: la cuenta de Instagram de Portugal cae a 24,6 millones de seguidores tras polémica
articles.text:
La cuenta de Instagram de la selección de Portugal está perdiendo seguidores en medio de la polémica con Cristiano Ronaldo y de momento, va en 24,6 millones de seguidores. Anteriormente estaba con un poco más de 25 de millones de usuarios.
La caída se produjo después de que el futbolista anunciara que abandonó el campo de entrenamiento de la selección tras una rueda de prensa del entrenador y una conversación con el presidente de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol.
PUBLICIDAD
En una publicación de Instagram, Ronaldo explicó:
“Después de la rueda de prensa del entrenador de la Selección Nacional, y tras una conversación con el presidente de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol, decidí abandonar el campo de entrenamiento de la Selección”.
“A su debido tiempo contaré la verdad a todos los portugueses sobre las razones que me motivaron a dejar la selección, a la que siempre me dediqué. Ahora es el momento de desear buena suerte a Portugal y a todos mis compañeros de equipo, sin excepción”, agregó.
Los mensajes de apoyo a Cristiano Ronaldo
La publicación de Cristiano Ronaldo reunió mensajes de respaldo de usuarios que cuestionaron el trato de la selección portuguesa hacia el delantero. “Por ti y solo por ti le iba a esa selección”, escribió la usuaria gabygabyr_, quien agregó que era “una lástima” cómo trataban a “su única estrella”.
PUBLICIDAD
Otro comentario, publicado por sebbastif, sostuvo: “Sos el mejor del mundo aquí y en todos lados, si te vas de Portugal todos dejamos de ser hinchas de Portugal”.
Las reacciones también aparecieron en el último post de la selección de Portugal. “Ronaldo es más grande que tu historia”, escribió el usuario 4j.3, mientras que dudeyusuf aseguró: “No te apoyaré más si no hay Ronaldo”. Otro usuario reclamó: “Cristiano Ronaldo es el que puso a Portugal en el mapa del mundo del fútbol”.
Cristiano Ronaldo es el futbolista con más seguidores
Cristiano Ronaldo es el futbolista más seguido en Instagram, donde reúne 679 millones de seguidores. Su perfil se convirtió en una de las principales vitrinas digitales de su carrera, con publicaciones centradas en el fútbol y en distintos aspectos de su vida personal.
PUBLICIDAD
La cuenta del delantero portugués registra 4.138 publicaciones y sigue a 636 perfiles. La cifra de seguidores lo ubica por encima de cualquier otro futbolista en la plataforma.
El perfil de Cristiano Ronaldo combina imágenes de sus entrenamientos, partidos y celebraciones con publicaciones junto a integrantes de su familia, además de contenidos vinculados a sus actividades fuera de las canchas.
En sus publicaciones más recientes aparecen imágenes de sus entrenamientos y encuentros con Al Nassr, el club con el que disputa sus partidos. También comparte fotos junto a sus compañeros y publicaciones vinculadas a su preparación física.
Ronaldo utiliza Instagram para mostrar su actividad con la selección de Portugal, incluidos los momentos previos a los partidos y las concentraciones del equipo.
Además del fútbol, el delantero publica fotos de su vida cotidiana, reuniones familiares y vehículos de lujo. Esa variedad de contenidos sostiene la interacción de una comunidad que supera los 679 millones de seguidores.
PUBLICIDAD
Messi es el segundo futbolista con más seguidores
Lionel Messi es el segundo futbolista más seguido en Instagram, con 516 millones de seguidores. Su cuenta reúne 1.543 publicaciones y sigue a 369 perfiles.
La cifra lo ubica detrás de Cristiano Ronaldo, cuya cuenta supera los 679 millones de seguidores. Ambos concentran las comunidades más numerosas entre los futbolistas en la plataforma.
El perfil de Messi combina contenidos de su actividad deportiva con publicaciones vinculadas a su vida fuera de las canchas y a sus proyectos comerciales.
Entre sus publicaciones recientes hay imágenes de partidos y celebraciones con la camiseta de Inter Miami, además de fotos junto a otras personas en el campo de juego.
PUBLICIDAD
El futbolista también comparte contenidos relacionados con la selección argentina, como una imagen en la que aparece con una camiseta celeste y blanca frente a una bandera del país.
Además, su perfil incluye anuncios de productos y publicaciones personales, como fotografías de reuniones y momentos familiares.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Apple CoreGraphics PoC Emerges as WhatsApp PDF Checks Hint at Possible Delivery Path
articles.text:
Security researchers have published the first public proof-of-concept for CVE-2026-86950, an Apple CoreGraphics flaw Apple says may have been used in attacks against specific targeted individuals.
The trigger is a malicious PDF with a crafted embedded font that crashes unpatched iPhones and Macs. The code causes a crash, not an execution error. Turning the memory corruption into a working exploit is separate work the analysis does not demonstrate.
Apple patched the flaw on September 28, crediting Meta Product Security with the discovery and noting it may have been used in an "extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27."
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the following day, requiring federal agencies to apply the fix by October 2.
Apple has not listed iOS 27 or macOS Golden Gate 27 as affected in the September 28 advisories. No workaround has been described for systems that cannot update immediately.
What the Researchers Found
The analysis was published September 30 by Dion Blazakis, Josh Maine, and Anna Groza of Calif, a firm known for research into zero-click attack surfaces in messaging apps. They started from a publicly available binary comparison of iOS 26.7 and 26.7.1.
CoreGraphics is the Apple framework for 2D drawing, image rendering, and PDF processing. It was the only library changed in 26.7.1, with the same fix applied more than 20 times across eight rasterizer functions.
The patched code converts a glyph coordinate from floating-point to a 32-bit fixed-point value. Before the patch, two of the eight functions handled out-of-range values differently: one saturated the result, the other truncated it.
That difference caused the calculated bounding box for a glyph to be too narrow. CoreGraphics then allocated a working buffer smaller than the edges it needed to draw, and wrote outside it.
To trigger the bug, the researchers built a TrueType font with coordinates large enough to force the overflow. Embedding it in a PDF with a text matrix and nested composite-glyph scaling pushes those coordinates past the limit. They published the generation scripts and a sample PDF in a public GitHub repository.
The harness calls the same ImageIO thumbnail path an app uses when previewing a received attachment. The researchers say the crash occurs on both macOS and iOS.
The macOS result includes a full debugger call stack. The iOS claim is Calif's, with no separate trace published.
The crash exposes a controlled out-of-bounds write that affects two adjacent 16-bit values in a buffer that the attacker can control, allowing writes to the stack or heap. Calif says converting that primitive into working code execution is separate work. Calif did not obtain the in-the-wild sample and cannot say how the attacker completed the chain.
The WhatsApp Question
Calif examined WhatsApp because Meta Product Security was credited with finding the flaw. The firm compared two recent WhatsApp versions, 26.37.73 and 26.38.74, and found new code in WhatsApp's Kaleidoscope attachment scanner.
The newer version reads PDF files for embedded font streams and flags suspicious ones with three defect tags: MalformedFontProgram, UndecodableFontProgram, and UnverifiedFontProgram. Any such tag returns a high-risk score to WhatsApp's attachment checker, which then stops automatic parsing of the flagged file.
Calif described those changes as circumstantial evidence pointing toward WhatsApp as a possible delivery vector. The firm's post describes its research as covering a possible WhatsApp zero-click path.
The published analysis does not describe or test a WhatsApp delivery path. The initial version did: it said the researchers' analysis suggested WhatsApp could deliver a PDF that triggers the flaw when a victim opens a chat from a trusted contact with automatic media downloads on.
That sentence was removed 85 minutes after publication in a commit by Calif CEO Thai Duong, who described the change as removing the WhatsApp speculation.
The analysis closes with a question: whether the flaw "was combined with additional vulnerabilities in WhatsApp to reach parsing with less user interaction." That phrasing suggests the path Calif studied would require user action or further WhatsApp vulnerabilities in the chain.
WhatsApp has published no advisory linking this flaw to its products. Its 2026 advisory page lists two unrelated vulnerabilities.
The Hacker News asked Meta whether WhatsApp was involved in the reported attacks. Meta did not respond before publication.
An earlier case makes the hypothesis plausible. In August 2025, WhatsApp assessed that a flaw in its linked-device synchronization messages may have been combined with a separate Apple out-of-bounds write and used against fewer than 200 targeted users, a pair of vulnerabilities THN covered at the time.
The Hacker News asked Calif about the removed delivery claim and whether the researchers had obtained the in-the-wild sample since publication. Calif did not respond before publication.
No network indicators, attacker identifiers, or exploit payload names have been made public. Apple has not said whether Lockdown Mode would have blocked the delivery path used in the reported attacks.

articles.title: Steam Deck 2: Is AMD Gainsborough the chip Valve’s been waiting for?
articles.text:
The Steam Deck is four and a half years old, and handheld gamers are eagerly awaiting a Steam Deck 2 — but Valve has consistently said it needs a new chip with a “generational leap” in performance and efficiency before building the sequel.
Steam Deck 2: Is AMD Gainsborough the chip Valve’s been waiting for?
There’s reason to be skeptical.
There’s reason to be skeptical.
There’s some reason to believe that chip has now broken cover: AMD Gainsborough. But I’m a tad skeptical.
As leaker Moore’s Law is Dead and IT Home report, the latest AMD drivers have leaked the codename for a previously unknown chip: an “AMD Gainsborough.” The first Steam Deck chip was named “Aerith” after Final Fantasy VII’s heartbreaking love interest, and Gainsborough is her last name. Plus, the chip appears to be a semi-custom one (read: designed for a specific customer) on TSMC’s relatively recent N3P process.
IT Home checked import/export records and found that AMD’s already been shipping test equipment for the Gainsborough chip for validation, suggesting that a potential customer might already be testing to see if it’s suitable for their device.
Those import records also show the Gainsborough chip will be fairly small, with an FF6 package measuring 25mm by 25mm. Today, leaker Gotou_3rd seemingly revealed that AMD’s next handheld chips, the Ryzen Z3 and Z3 Extreme, will also be 25mm by 25mm chips. Gotou also published a possible fragment of an AMD slide deck that suggests the Z3 is targeting 15 watts, the same power envelope as the Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED:
This isn’t quite enough to tie Gainsborough specifically to a Steam Deck 2, though.
First, a semi-custom chip doesn’t always wind up in its originally intended gadget. It’s long been rumored that the Steam Deck’s own semi-custom chip wasn’t originally designed for the Steam Deck, but rather a Magic Leap headset, and that it was shopped around for tablets (including this canceled Microsoft tablet, the story goes) before Valve took advantage. There are portions of the original Steam Deck’s chip that went entirely unused.
Second, you should know that “Aerith” (Steam Deck), “Sephiroth” (Steam Deck OLED) and “Gainsborough” are not Valve’s codenames. When I visited Valve’s headquarters in late 2023, I commented on this Aerith wafer hanging on the wall — and Valve designers told me they didn’t really want the Final Fantasy codenames. AMD was the one that chose them.
Some extra evidence that Valve isn’t tied to those names: When Microsoft and Asus picked the “Ryzen Z2 A” chip for the vanilla $500 Xbox Ally, they were choosing an “Aerith Plus” chip.
Third, 25mm by 25mm might be small, but it’s actually large for a Steam Deck! The original Steam Deck’s “Aerith” chip, before it shrunk to remove the unused components in its “Sephiroth” revision, reportedly measured 19mm by 19mm. But perhaps Gainsborough is efficient, and perhaps it’s more affordable if this apple doesn’t fall too far from AMD’s 25mm x 25mm Ryzen Z3 tree.
Lastly, Valve was still figuring out “how and when” to do a Steam Deck 2 as of last month, after it would have theoretically received these Gainsborough chips. But I guess Valve might just be trying not to overpromise, after this year’s RAM-forced hardware delays.

articles.title: AOC reveals a 1,000Hz gaming monitor that's due early next year, begging the question — how much is too much with refresh rates?
articles.text:
AOC reveals a 1,000Hz gaming monitor — but do you really need anything like that high a refresh rate?
A rate of knots
- AOC has revealed the Agon Pro AGP257FT, a 24.5-inch Full HD monitor
- It has a native 1,000Hz refresh rate
- Expect this gaming monitor to debut in Q1 2027, but we don't have a price yet
AOC has announced a new gaming monitor which runs at a native 1,000Hz refresh rate.
TechPowerUp posted the press release for the Agon Pro AGP257FT, which is a 24.5-inch Full HD IPS monitor offering a response time of 0.3ms (grey-to-grey) and DisplayHDR 400 support.
As mentioned, it runs natively at 1,000Hz, meaning you get that refresh rate out of the box (and there's no dual mode here, where a monitor has two refresh rate settings with different resolutions, dropping the latter to achieve the faster rate).
You get 1,000Hz at 1920 x 1080 resolution, with an overclock option to push the refresh rate slightly further to 1,050Hz.
The AGP257FT is an oxide-based 'Fast IPS' panel that has 20-zone local dimming and 90% coverage of the DCI-P3 color gamut (and 99% coverage for sRGB), with a brightness of 450 nits.
The monitor supports Nvidia G-Sync and has an adjustable stand (allowing for 150mm of range in height) with tilt, swivel and pivot (complete with markings to keep a favored position).
You get two HDMI 2.1 ports along with a DisplayPort 2.1 connector and a headphone output, plus a USB hub (sporting a trio of USB-A ports). There's a headset hook here, too.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The Agon Pro AGP257FT monitor is set to arrive in Q1 2027, with pricing still to be confirmed.
Analysis: rating the rate
Don't expect this to be a cheap monitor. With the 1,000Hz refresh rate, this is aimed at professional esports gamers, so it'll exact quite the toll on your wallet. Especially given that even monitors aren't immune to the price hikes we've seen across all sorts of tech thanks to the pressures of the RAM crisis and global geopolitical climate (affecting shipping).
Of course, do you really need a 1,000Hz screen even if you are a competitive gamer? Perhaps it's justifiable from some viewpoints, but unless money really is no object with your gaming setup, it's going to be major overkill for most people.
For starters, you're not going to get 1,000 frames per second (to match that 1,000Hz refresh rate) even on esports shooters with a top-end PC – remembering that it's not just a matter of reaching or peaking at that level, but sustaining it (on average).
Okay, so it is also true that there are still benefits in terms of a smoother image with less motion blur, and less input lag, when running at 1,000Hz, even if your frames per second aren't up at that level – so this tech isn't wasted in this scenario.
Still, whether the price of these kinds of screens is worth it is, shall we say, highly debatable. Besides which, in the case of this AOC monitor gamers will argue that IPS isn't the best choice if you want motion clarity anyway, and that you'd be better off looking at, say, a 720Hz OLED (which is still a blazingly fast refresh rate).
The vast majority of gamers will be better off focusing their expenditure on the PC itself, though – and there's certainly a need for the extra money given the RAM crisis – rather than pushing out the boat for a monitor which probably only offers minor advantages in the end (unless you're actually a pro gamer).

articles.title: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
articles.text:
A federal judge has dismissed a pair of antitrust lawsuits filed by Chegg and Rolling Stone parent company Penske Media Corporation, which accused Google of driving away web traffic with its AI-powered search features, as reported earlier by Reuters. US District Judge Amit Mehta takes Google’s side in a ruling on Wednesday, writing that PMC and Chegg’s claims don’t stand up to antitrust law.
Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
Rolling Stone’s parent company and Chegg claimed Google’s AI search features drove away traffic from their sites.
In lawsuits filed last year, Chegg and PMC accused Google of abusing its monopoly power by coercing publishers into supplying content for AI Overviews for free, or risk disappearing from search results. The publishers alleged Google’s practices diverted traffic away from their sites, hurting their revenue.
Judge Mehta, who made a landmark antitrust ruling against Google in 2024, disagrees with Chegg and PMC’s claims. “Plaintiffs have pleaded only that they have an ‘expectation’ that Google will send them search traffic if they make their content available for free,” Mehta writes. “But an expectation is not an agreement. It is simply how a general search engine works.”
Mehta adds that the court is not “unsympathetic to the situation publishers now find themselves in,” but writes that antitrust rules can’t replace a legislative body’s decision to address the economic impact of “new innovation.”
Meanwhile, publishers continue to see effects of Google’s AI-powered search overhaul, with traffic to news outlets and small websites taking a steep dive. This week, The Information reported that Google is paying around 100 publishers for their contributions to AI Overviews, AI Mode, and Gemini as part of a pilot program.
Disclosure: The Verge is part of Penske Media.

articles.title: Mitigating Threats With Pre-Silicon Security Verification
articles.text:
The types of threats that must be mitigated and a process to verify that designs are secure in real-world deployment.
The safety and security of the silicon chips ubiquitous in modern life have become prime considerations in semiconductor development. Functional safety is well understood, with numerous industry standards and a variety of established mechanisms embedded in silicon to ensure that systems do not misbehave due to environmental conditions or aging. Security is an equally important concern, but techniques to design secure chips have emerged relatively recently. This post discusses the types of threats that must be mitigated and a process to verify that designs are secure in real-world deployment.
Advocates for functional safety often cite the example of a chip failure causing an autonomous vehicle to crash. Just as this motivates designers to consider safety mechanisms, the specter of a malicious agent taking control of a vehicle and intentionally crashing it is equally terrifying. There have already been demonstrations that such actions are possible in certain cases. System-level security is often thought of as a software problem, such as preventing denial of service (DOS) and buffer overflow attacks. However, hardware-level threats must also be considered.
Silicon security is a complex topic. Preventing an agent from accessing a chip and altering its behavior is the goal, but there are at least two types of scenarios to consider. The first is making a system misbehave, such as the car crash example. Not all scenarios are this dramatic, but they still must be avoided. These include a burglar electronically unlocking a door, a competitor disabling the cooling system in a company’s warehouse, and a voyeur hacking into a webcam or smart speaker to spy on someone. Secure silicon means preventing all these bad situations.
The other type of security failure scenario is compromising private information. Data breaches can be due to unauthorized hardware access as well as software attacks. Personal identifiers, financial information, medical records, and other sensitive data can be compromised if the chips allow illegal access. Semiconductor designers must ensure that their devices remain secure in the presence of real-world threats, preventing both external control of systems and release of private information to the outside.
Humans have been hacking electronic systems for as long as they have existed, but the rise of the Internet meant that physical access was no longer required. The risk is now increasing even more with the rise of agentic AI. Several examples of agents under test breaking into other systems over the Internet have been in the news lately. There is every reason to believe that malicious actors will increasingly use AI agents for their attacks. This makes it more critical than ever to design secure chips.
Another challenge of silicon security is the wide range of ways that malicious agents can try to gain access. Sometimes called threat vectors, these methods vary over the silicon lifecycle and affect many parts of the semiconductor supply chain. At the architectural and RTL design stages, “Trojans” might be inserted into the design by a rogue designer or inadvertently incorporated via a third-party IP block. Someone who knows how to access and trigger a hardware Trojan can potentially make the chip do undesirable things.
Trojans can also potentially be inserted during design implementation, for example during logic synthesis or the place and route process. During the manufacturing process, wafer probing might reveal unintended data to aid in reverse engineering or cloning the design. Once the chip is included in an end product and deployed in the field, the scariest scenarios emerge. Trojans can be activated, side-channel leakage such as power and voltage variations can reveal private data, and faults can be injected via lasers, electromagnetic pulses, or power supply glitching.
Developing a secure chip that can mitigate all the threat vectors and scenarios outlined above is far from a simple proposition. It requires the support of many EDA tools in the development flow. The process starts with assessing possible threats, deciding how to model them, and developing a set of security requirements. The design phase includes using a set of reusable security IP components, each pre-verified, pre-certified, and silicon-proven. The designers certainly don’t want to introduce Trojans via IP that claims to improve silicon security.
The chip assembly process must ensure that these components are connected properly to provide their intended benefits. As the design evolves, it must be analyzed by advanced checks that look for security weaknesses. The verification phase employs a combination of static, formal, and simulation techniques to identify vulnerabilities to possible threats. Finally, implementation (layout, equivalence checking, static timing analysis, and power computation) must preserve security and ensure final hardware is tamper-proof. The result is end-to-end design, verification, and implementation for secure chip development with tamper-proof assurance.
Both the designers and the verification team play key roles in developing a secure chip design. Together, they develop a security verification plan in addition to a functional verification plan. They identify the parts of the design where security is critical, including registers holding private data and access points for secure blocks. The designers choose appropriate security IP and employ a variety of techniques to protect the critical portions of the design. They also run RTL-level linting and other static checks for potential design vulnerabilities.
Going beyond static checks requires the analytic power of formal verification and the scaling of simulation and emulation. The designers may assist in this effort, but it is mainly driven by the dedicated verification team. Formal methods can perform deeper analysis on the design to check for security issues. Formal verification can be applied early in the development process since no testbench is required, but it works best at the block level. For full SoC verification, simulation using constrained-random testbenches and functional coverage metrics is the primary solution.
Pre-silicon security verification has several goals:
Synopsys provides a complete solution for implementing secure silicon by design and for verifying that it can mitigate real-world threats in the field. The process starts with the Synopsys IP portfolio, which includes functionality such as root of trust, secure boot, secure keying, secure processing, secure interfaces, encryption, decryption, and authentication. These IP blocks are all inherently secure and validated by use in many previous chips. Of course, they must be connected properly into the overall design to provide the desired protection.
The designers write a lot of RTL code and integrate other types of IP blocks, and it is essential to know that all of this has been coded in a way that does not make them vulnerable to security threats. This is accomplished by checking for such vulnerabilities during the early RTL phase using the security checks in the Synopsys VC SpyGlass RTL static signoff platform. These checks do not require special verification knowledge and can be run easily by the designers every time they make RTL modifications.
The second phase of verification addresses the security of data at rest and in motion. For sign-off, the verification team must have evidence that security-critical data cannot be read illegally and leaked to unsecured destinations (confidentiality) or written from an unsecured source (integrity). The Formal Security Verification (FSV) app for Synopsys VC Formal verifies data security and prevents data leaks or integrity violations for sensitive data such as encryption keys, passwords, and biometric information inside secure modules.
The Synopsys VCS simulator has taint propagation (T-Prop) functionality that enables users to set, trace, and monitor “taints” that act as proxies for malicious attacks. This allows RTL simulation to verify how taints travel through the design (permeability) and how long they remain in the system (permanence). Simulation with taints detects design bugs that lead to security issues. The Synopsys Verdi debug and verification management solution displays taint simulation results in a way that is easy to understand.
The final step in verification security entails checking the design’s resiliency to tampering, such as high-precision bit-flips using laser fault injection. Modeling faults due to such attacks leverages the well-established methods for modeling manufacturing faults. The Synopsys VC Z01X fault injection and simulation solution shows the effects of these faults and verifies that they cannot compromise security at the silicon level.
Security is no longer a distant relative of functional safety: it is now a primary concern for semiconductors in many end applications. The complete development flow must ensure that the result is hardware that can do its job in the field without being vulnerable to attacks or leakage of private data. Verification using static, formal, and simulation methods is a key part of this process. The Synopsys pre-silicon security verification solution is a proven way to produce secure chips. A white paper is available with more details.

articles.title: Otto Days im Preis-Check: So viel sparst du bei Macbook, iPad und Co.
articles.text:
Otto Days: Lohnen sich die Apple-Angebote wirklich?
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Am 6. und 7. Oktober finden bei Amazon wieder die Prime Deal Days statt. Mit diesem exklusives Shopping-Event für Prime-Mitglieder soll das Vorweihnachtsgeschäft eingeläutet werden. Jetzt zieht Otto als zweitgrößter Online-Marktplatz Deutschlands mit Angeboten in Kategorien wie Mode, Möbel und Haushaltsgeräte nach. Hier soll jede:r sparen können – soweit zumindest das Versprechen. Auch viele Apple-Geräte sind im Rahmen der Otto Days reduziert. Für alle, die über ein neues iPad oder eine Apple Watch nachdenken, könnte das also eine gute Gelegenheit sein, um ein bisschen Geld zu sparen. Wir haben die Otto-Angebote geprüft und verraten dir, ob sie sich wirklich für dich lohnen.
Deshalb sind viele Apple-Geräte jetzt teurer
Wer ein neues Macbook braucht oder sein Apple-Ökosystem erweitern möchte, muss jetzt deutlich tiefer in die Tasche greifen als noch vor einem halben Jahr. Grund dafür ist die Speicherkrise, die durch den KI-Boom ausgelöst wurde. Da die Ausstattung von KI-Rechenzentren für Chiphersteller oft lukrativer ist, haben viele ihre Produktion umgestellt. Dadurch werden SSDs und Arbeitsspeicher für Computer, Laptops und Smartphones knapper – und die Kosten steigen.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Auch Apple ist massiv von der anhaltenden Speicherkrise betroffen. „Wir haben noch nie erlebt, dass die Preise für Komponenten so stark und so schnell gestiegen sind. Bisher haben wir unsere Kund:innen von diesen Preissteigerungen verschont”, erklärte der Tech-Konzern im Juni gegenüber Reuters. „Jetzt haben wir allerdings einen Punkt erreicht, an dem wir die Preise für einige Produkte anheben müssen.“
Hier ist das Macbook Air gerade günstiger zu haben
Für die meisten ist das Macbook Air der beste Apple-Laptop für den Alltag. Es ist leistungsfähiger und langlebiger als das Macbook Neo, aber leichter und günstiger als das Macbook Pro. Das macht es zu einer idealen Wahl für Büro, Studium und mobiles Arbeiten. Apple hat die Preise zuletzt allerdings deutlich erhöht: So kostete das Gerät Anfang des Jahres noch 999 Dollar, im März stieg der Preis mit neuem M5-Chip und verdoppeltem Speicher auf 1.099 Dollar. Im Juni folgte eine weitere Preiserhöhung auf 1.299 Dollar – bei unveränderter Hardware. Auch in Deutschland sind die Kosten deutlich gestiegen.
Im Apple Store liegt der Einstiegspreis aktuell bei 1.399 Euro. Bei Amazon kostet das günstigste Angebot 1.247 Euro – rund 150 Euro weniger. Otto bietet das Notebook mit 10-Core-GPU und einem Terabyte internem Speicher aktuell für 1.499 Euro an. Diese Ausstattung lohnt sich für alle, die viele Fotos und Videos lokal speichern und regelmäßig grafiklastige Aufgaben erledigen möchten. Direkt bei Apple kostet das Macbook Air mit dieser Ausstattung 1.729 Euro. Bei Otto sparst du also 230 Euro. Bei Amazon ist der Apple-Laptop mit dieser Ausstattung allerdings schon ab 1.449 Euro erhältlich und damit noch günstiger zu haben.
Warum du beim iPad-Kauf lieber abwarten solltest
Auch das iPad ist in den vergangenen Monaten deutlich teurer geworden. Apple bietet verschiedene Modelle mit unterschiedlichen Displaygrößen, Leistungen und Ausstattungen an, um verschiedene Zielgruppen anzusprechen. Das Standard-iPad ist ein klassisches Einsteigsmodell, das sich ideal für den Alltag eignet. Es verfügt über ein elf Zoll großes Liquid-Retina-Display. Die Rückkamera liefert mit zwölf Megapixeln Videoaufnahmen in 4K-Qualität, während die Frontkamera Videotelefonie ermöglicht. Zusätzlich verfügt das Modell über Stereo-Lautsprecher und zwei Mikrofone.
Bei Apple kostet das iPad aktuell ab 499 Euro. Während es bis Juni in externen Shops noch regelmäßig für unter 330 Euro erhältlich war, müssen Käufer:innen laut etablierten Vergleichsportalen jetzt rund 100 Euro mehr zahlen. Otto bietet das Tablet aktuell zehn Prozent günstiger für 449 Euro an, auf Amazon sowie bei Media Markt und Saturn gilt derselbe Preis. Im Vergleich zur unverbindlichen Preisempfehlung lässt sich damit zwar sparen, allerdings ist das iPad regelmäßig günstiger zu haben. So war es im Juli auf Amazon kurzzeitig sogar auf unter 350 Euro reduziert. Wer wirklich sparen will, wartet daher besser ab.
Apple-Angebote: Die Otto Days lohnen sich nicht
Otto hat derzeit zahlreiche weitere Apple-Geräte als Angebot ausgezeichnet. Bei vielen davon, wie etwa der Apple Watch, fällt der Preisnachlass allerdings nur gering aus. Auch Zubehör wie die Magic Mouse oder die kabelgebundenen Earpods sind reduziert. Wie der Preisvergleich zeigt, sind diese in anderen Shops aber oft günstiger zu haben. Wer den besten Deal erzielen möchte, sollte vermeintliche Angebote deshalb unbedingt auf Vergleichsportalen prüfen. Dabei zeigt sich oft, dass die Schnäppchen gar nicht so gut sind, wie es auf den ersten Blick erscheint. Das bestätigt sich auch beim Check der Apple-Angebote im Rahmen der Otto Days.

articles.title: Une nouvelle fuite de données frappe l'État français, et l’Anssi fait partie des victimes
articles.text:
L’Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d’information (Anssi) a elle-même été victime d’une fuite de données. Dans un rapport publié ce 30 septembre 2026, l’agence révèle que son laboratoire d’innovation a été touché par une cyberattaque. Il s’agit de l’équipe interne de l’agence qui doit aider les entreprises, les collectivités et les particuliers à mieux se protéger. C’est également le cas de la Direction interministérielle du numérique (Dinum), le service de l’État français chargé de la transformation numérique et de la transmission de données entre organismes publics.
 📄 L’ANSSI publie un premier point de situation de l’opération REACTIV.
➡️Plus d’informations sur :https://t.co/BPognC5Afw pic.twitter.com/kayoegqayd
— ANSSI (@ANSSI_FR) September 30, 2026
À lire aussi : Piratage des impôts – l’ANSSI révèle ce qu’il s’est vraiment passé lors de la cyberattaque
Une faille dans Metabase à l’origine de l’attaque
L’offensive remonte au 6 août 2026. Ce jour-là, Metabase, le logiciel qui sert à analyser des données et à créer des tableaux de bord, annonce que ses systèmes ont été compromis à la suite d’une intrusion. De nombreuses organisations, publiques comme privées, s’appuient sur Metabase pour suivre leurs statistiques.
En exploitant la faille, les pirates ont pu récupérer des accès à des comptes de l’Anssi et de la Dinum. La brèche a été rapidement corrigée par Metabase. Ces dernières semaines, la même faille a été exploitée contre Shipup, le prestataire de Carrefour, et contre la plateforme publique Zéro Logement Vacant, ou encore contre des services de cryptomonnaies, dont Trezor.
118 comptes touchés à l’Anssi
Du côté de l’Anssi, 118 comptes d’utilisateurs ont été compromis au sein du laboratoire d’innovation de l’agence. Une trentaine de comptes appartiennent à des personnes extérieures à l’agence. Avec les comptes volés, les pirates ont mis la main sur des identifiants, des adresses e-mail, des statistiques d’utilisation et des mots de passe transformés en caractères illisibles.
Deux instances Metabase utilisées par la Dinum ont aussi été piratées. L’une des instances est liée à ProConnect. Ce service de l’État, géré par la Dinum, permet aux agents publics et aux professionnels de se connecter à de nombreux services publics avec une seule identité professionnelle. La seconde instance est liée à Nuage-Public, le marché public interministériel du cloud.
Les données dérobées comprennent surtout des informations administratives (numéros SIREN et SIRET, budgets, effectifs), des métadonnées de projets, et des historiques de connexion anonymisés. Selon l’Anssi, ces données sont déjà publiques. Depuis l’intrusion, l’Anssi a mis à jour toutes les instances vulnérables et renouvelé tous les mots de passe. L’agence a aussi désactivé tous les comptes qui étaient inactifs depuis au moins trois mois. Même son de cloche du côté de la Dinum, qui a corrigé les failles, réinitialisé les accès et supprimé les comptes créés par les pirates.
99 fuites de données présumées à l’État
L’affaire tombe à un mauvais moment pour l’Anssi. Un jour plus tôt, l’agence a publié un rapport très critique sur le piratage de la Direction générale des finances publiques, qui a touché près de 700 000 personnes cet été. L’agence pointait notamment du doigt le manque de vigilance des impôts face à la récupération massive de données.
En amont de ces nouvelles attaques, le Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, a reconnu que « peu de ministères sont au niveau requis » en matière de cybersécurité. Il a notamment demandé à l’ANSSI de mettre au point une équipe d’intervention d’urgence, « Reponse & Action Interministérielle face aux Violations de données » (REACTIV). Le premier bilan de ce dispositif a dénombré 99 fuites de données présumées dans les services de l’État depuis le 1ᵉʳ août 2026. Après vérification, 67 des violations ont été confirmées. Plus d’une trentaine de fuites sont toujours traitées par les agents de REACTIV.
